However, only GoogleCalendarService uses credentialId to select the right calendar (`find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`); BaseCalendarService and the other providers were only updated to destructure the first entry (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` in packages/lib/CalendarService.ts, LarkCalendarService, Office365CalendarService) and use its externalId for all calls. So when multiple destination calendars exist, non-Google providers will create the event in the first calendar regardless of which credential is being used — the per-credential loop in EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents will target the wrong calendar. The mechanism is verifiable in the diff; severity of real-world impact is somewhat uncertain, but it is a genuine defect introduced by the array migration.

record.issue_text: [Medium/bug] BaseCalendarService (CalendarManager.ts / CalendarService.ts) — `createEvent`/`listCalendars` also only use `destinationCalendar[0]` and ignore `credentialId`; per-credential loop will create events into the wrong calendar for non-Google providers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `destinationCalendar` to an array and updates Google to select the calendar by `credentialId`, but `BaseCalendarService` (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts) still derives behavior solely from the first element: it destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then filters/marks calendars using only `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (both in `createEvent`-path filtering and `listCalendars` primary flag). There is no selection by the `credentialId` passed from `CalendarManager.createEvent` (`calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`), so when `EventManager` loops per destination/credential, non-Google providers using this base logic can apply the wrong `externalId` (from destinationCalendar[0]) for a different credential.
